page: OVHcloud t1-45 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud instance within the Cloud GPU family. The system is provisioned with 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. System memory totals 45.0 GB of RAM, offering approximately 5.62 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single dedicated NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is provisioned at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward parallel GPU acceleration rather than raw host CPU processing. CPU single-core metrics fall into the bottom 25th percentile across Geekbench and stress-ng evaluations, reflecting the lower single-thread throughput of the Intel Xeon Silver 4214. Multi-core compute and memory bandwidth fall firmly in the median range, with multi-core Geekbench scoring 5,414. In contrast, deep learning benchmarks show top-tier execution on the Volta GPU: prompt processing for a 7B parameter model achieves 1,313.81 tokens per second, and text generation reaches 118.24 tokens per second, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD and dedicated 16 GB VRAM GPU provide a balanced environment for mid-scale AI and computational jobs without requiring auxiliary disk provisioning. However, host-bound serial tasks face architectural bottlenecks due to modest CPU clock speeds and single-thread throughput. The 16 GB frame buffer also limits native execution of very large models without aggressive quantization or offloading, as evidenced by low throughput on 70B parameter prompt processing.

OVHcloud t1-45 is well suited for targeted deep learning inference, model fine-tuning of medium-sized networks, computer vision, data engineering pipelines, and GPU-accelerated scientific computing that fit within a 16 GB VRAM budget.
